title: Synthesis and Characterisation of Thiophene-Functionalised Lanthanoid Diketonate Clusters with Solvent-Modulated Europium Luminescence

synthesis.procedure: General lanthanoid cluster synthesis: Hhtp (230 mg, 1.0 mmol) and hydrated lanthanoid chloride (0.5 mmol) were dissolved in methanol (ca. 20 mL) in a round-bottomed flask. Triethylamine (1 mL) was added dropwise over 15 min and the mixture was stirred for 12 h. In some cases product precipitated and was collected by filtration then recrystallised. Otherwise the solvent was removed, the residue was stirred in toluene (ca. 2 mL) for 1 h, filtered to remove triethylammonium salts, and left in an open vial to slowly concentrate, yielding orange crystals of 1 harvested before complete solvent loss. An excess of triethylamine was used.
synthesis.time: 15 min base addition, then 12 h stirring; residue stirred 1 h in toluene
synthesis.vessel_or_method: round-bottomed flask with stirrer bead; slow concentration in open vial
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: optional filtration of precipitate and recrystallisation; otherwise solvent removal, stirring in toluene, filtration of triethylammonium salts, and slow concentration to orange crystals

properties.summary: Cluster 2 is strongly quenched in chloroform at 25 °C (emission barely above background) due to thermal population of a ligand-to-metal charge-transfer state above 0 °C. Characteristic Eu(III) emission is observed with excitation at 312 nm and emission monitored at 613 nm (5D0→7FJ, J=0–4). Coordinating solvents restore luminescence while the tetranuclear motif remains intact (FTIR/Raman): pyridine gives a linear intensity increase up to 188 equiv. (R2=0.9982) and a 30-fold increase at 625 equiv.; DMSO and DMF enhance emission with shorter linear ranges (0–22 and 0–33 equiv.); dioxane gives ca. 4-fold enhancement at 356 equiv. Demonstrated room-temperature luminescent sensing of pyridine, DMF and DMSO.
